landing.badge: Open source · MIT · Self-hostable · No cookies
landing.heroBody: metrics counts page views and visitors for every project you register: top pages, referrers, countries and cities, devices, browsers and custom events — from one script tag, a pixel or an API call. No cookies, no stored IP addresses, nothing to put in a consent banner.
landing.freeNote: Free plan: {projects} projects & {events} events / month. No card required.
landing.pathsBody: Pick the one that fits each app. They all land in the same dashboard.
landing.pathScriptBody: Under 3 KB, no dependencies. Counts every page view, follows single-page-app route changes, and exposes metrics.track() for custom events. Works in Qwik, Astro, React, jQuery pages and Phaser games alike.
landing.pathPixelBody: A 1×1 image for places where JavaScript can't run: emails, READMEs, documentation hosted elsewhere. The URL says which page or event it stands for.
landing.pathApiBody: A single POST with the project's public key, from your backend, a CLI, a game server or a cron job. Perfect for apps without a DOM.
landing.step1Body: One project per site or app. You get a public key for the script, the pixel and the API, and you pick its time zone.
landing.step2Body: Copy it from the project settings into your layout. The first page views show up within seconds.
landing.step3Body: Pick a range, click any page, country or device to filter everything by it, watch the live counter, or let an AI agent read the numbers through MCP.
landing.seeTitle: Everything you want to know, nothing you don't
landing.seeBody: The dashboard answers the questions people actually ask about a site, and stops there.
landing.seeWhereBody: Referrers, UTM source / medium / campaign, countries, regions and cities.
landing.seeWhoBody: Desktop, mobile or tablet; browser and operating system; screen size and language.
landing.seeWhatBody: Top pages, entry paths, and the custom events you send (signups, purchases, clicks) with their properties.
landing.seeLiveBody: Visitors in the last five minutes and the pages they are on.
landing.privacyBody: The tracker sets no cookie and writes nothing to the browser. The server hashes each visitor's IP address with a salt that changes every day, keeps only the derived country, region and city, and throws the user agent away once device, browser and OS are known.
landing.privacy1: No cookies, no localStorage, no fingerprinting across sites or days
landing.privacy2: Raw IP addresses are never stored — only a daily salted hash
landing.privacy3: Query strings are dropped from page URLs (except UTM tags), so tokens and emails never reach the dashboard
landing.privacy4: Optional Do Not Track support, and bots are filtered out
landing.apiNote: Public keys can only send hits. They can never read anything.
landing.mcpTitle: Ask your AI agent how the site is doing
landing.mcpIntro: metrics ships an MCP server. Connect it to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP host and ask things like
landing.mcpExample1: “how did traffic to the docs change this week?”
landing.mcpExample2: “which countries visit the pricing page most?”
landing.mcpBullet1Body: A viewer key never even sees the delete tools; editor and admin unlock more. Enforced by the API too.
landing.mcpBullet2Body: Destructive actions (delete a project, purge its events) ask you to confirm before anything happens.
landing.selfhostBody1: The entire stack — Flask API, tracker, MCP server and this Qwik app — is MIT-licensed. Run it on your own VPS with one
landing.ctaTitle: See your first visitor in a minute
landing.ctaBody: Create a project, paste one script tag and watch the live counter move.

pricing.intro: Start free. Upgrade when you need more projects, more events per month or longer retention. Self-host for unlimited everything.
pricing.earlyBody: Unlimited projects, events and retention, the API and the MCP server. When plans arrive we will announce it on the blog and by email before any limit applies to an existing account. Prices and limits below may still change.
pricing.footnote: All prices in USD. Annual billing saves ~20%. Project and key counts are hard limits; events over the monthly budget are counted but not stored, and your site never sees an error. Events older than the retention window are pruned.
docs.intro: How to put metrics in your app, send hits from anywhere, and read the numbers through the REST API or an AI agent. The full contract — every endpoint, object and error — lives in the repository.
docs.trackerBody: A zero-dependency script under 3 KB served from this host. Add it once in your layout; it sends one hit per page view and per single-page-app route change, with no cookies and nothing stored in the browser.
docs.attrSpa: hook the History API and send a page view on every route change. Set to false to call metrics.pageview() yourself.
docs.attrHash: hash routing: keep the #fragment in the URL and listen to hashchange.
docs.attrDnt: honour the browser's Do Not Track signal.
docs.attrLocal: also track on localhost, raw IPs, file: and *.local (ignored by default).
docs.attrApi: override the collect endpoint (self-hosted instances behind another host).
docs.trackerJsBody: window.metrics exposes track(name, props) for custom events and pageview() for manual page views. Calls queued before the script loads are replayed.
docs.trackerDeclarative: Clicks on elements with data-metrics-event are tracked automatically, with optional JSON props:
docs.trackerWhat: What is sent: the page URL without its query string (UTM tags are read and then dropped), the referrer, the title, the screen size and the browser language. Device, browser, OS and location are derived on the server from the request and never stored raw.
docs.pixelBody: For places where no JavaScript runs — newsletters, README files, documentation on another host. The image is a 43-byte transparent GIF, never cached. Pass the page as u and, optionally, an event name as n.
docs.collectBody: POST /api/collect with the project's public key in the X-Project-Key header (or a k field). JSON, form-encoded and text/plain bodies are accepted, CORS is open, and the answer is always 202 so a tracked site never sees an error.
docs.collectField1: n: event name (defaults to pageview). 1-60 letters, digits, spaces, _ . : / or -.
docs.collectField2: u: the page URL or path (required for anything meaningful). Query strings are only read for UTM tags.
docs.collectField3: r: referrer URL; t: page title (≤ 200); l: language (≤ 16); w / h: screen size.
docs.collectField4: p: a JSON object of properties for custom events (≤ 2 KB).
docs.collectField5: s: source — script (default), pixel or api. Device, browser, OS and location come from the request's own headers and address.
docs.collectResponses: The body says what happened: { ok: true } when stored, or { ok: false, reason } with reason = paused (tracking off for the project), origin (hostname not in the allowed list), bot (crawler or headless browser) or limit (over the monthly budget — counted, not stored).
docs.authApiKey: Management API: API keys with a role (viewer / editor / admin). Header X-API-Key: metrics_live_… (or Authorization: Bearer).
docs.authPublicKey: Collect API, tracker and pixel: project public keys. Header X-Project-Key: metrics_pub_… (or the k field). They identify one project and can only send hits.
docs.projectsBody: A project is one site or app. It owns a public key, a time zone (used to bucket days), an optional list of allowed hostnames, and the collect / bot switches.
docs.statsBody: Ranges are inclusive local dates in the tz parameter (default: the project's zone), as period=today|yesterday|7d|30d|90d|12mo or from/to. Any dimension can be passed as a filter (e.g. country=ES&device=mobile) and everything in the answer is scoped to it. Visitors are counted with a daily hash, so across several days they are daily uniques, summed.
docs.dimensionsBody: Usable as breakdown (by=) and as filters on every stats and events endpoint. referrer=(direct) selects hits with no referrer.
docs.errorsBody: Errors are JSON: { "error": { "code", "message" } }. Creating past a plan limit answers 402 limit_reached with error.which = projects | api_keys. Hits over the monthly event budget are accepted (202) but not stored.
docs.privacyBody: Privacy: metrics never stores raw IP addresses or user agents — only a salted daily hash and the derived device / browser / OS / location fields. Page URLs lose their query string before storage.
docs.mcpBody: The MCP server exposes the management API as tools, filtered by the role of the key you connect with. Destructive tools ask for confirmation. A weekly_report prompt walks a model through a project's numbers.
docs.mcpTools: Tools: list_projects, get_project, create_project, update_project, rotate_project_key, delete_project, project_summary, get_stats, get_breakdown, list_events, get_live, purge_events, get_usage, get_audit_log.

dash.empty: No projects yet. Create one per site or app to get its public key and install snippet.
overview.tzHint: The project's time zone; change it in Settings.
overview.vsPrevious: Compared with the previous period of the same length
overview.noGeo: No location data. Needs the GeoLite2 database on the server.
overview.noUtm: No UTM-tagged visits in this range.
overview.noEvents: No custom events yet. Send one with metrics.track().
overview.visitorsNote: Visitors are counted with a cookie-less daily hash, so over several days the number is the sum of daily unique visitors.
events.title: Title
events.privacyNote: The visitor column is a daily hash: it groups one person's hits within a day and nothing more.
psettings.installBody: Add the script to your layout, drop a pixel where no JavaScript runs, or post to the collect API from your backend.
psettings.publicKeyHint: Not a secret: it ships inside your site. It can only send hits. Rotate it if it gets abused, or restrict it with the allowed hostnames below.
psettings.snippetScriptHint: Counts every page view and single-page-app route change. Attributes and the JavaScript API:
psettings.snippetPixelHint: For emails and READMEs. u is the page or thing you want to count; add n=open for a named event. Details:
psettings.snippetEventsHint: Up to 2 KB of JSON props per event. They show up under Custom events and in the event log. Details:
psettings.snippetApiHint: From a backend, a CLI or a cron job. Device and location come from the request itself. Details:
psettings.trackingBody: What is accepted and how days are counted. Changes apply to the next hit.
psettings.geoOff: Location lookups are disabled globally right now; new hits are stored without country or city.
psettings.allowedOriginsHint: One per line, e.g. myapp.example.com or *.example.com. Empty = any host. Hits from other hosts are dropped.
psettings.purgeBody: Deletes every stored event of this project. The project and its key stay.
psettings.dangerBody: Deleting the project removes it and all its events. This cannot be undone.
